iast.description: International Alphabet of Sanskrit Transliteration (Latin with diacritics)

edge_cases.mixed_scripts: Use dominant script detection - prefer Devanagari if present
edge_cases.missing_diacritics: Warn but continue - treat as best guess approximation
edge_cases.latin_characters: Log as unrecognized - may be proper nouns or foreign terms

transliteration_confidence.hk_to_slp1: Medium - some ambiguity in consonant clusters

guru_conditions.long_vowel: Syllable with inherent long vowel (A:, I:, U:, R:, L:) is always Guru (G)
guru_conditions.vowel_before_conjunct: Short vowel before a conjunct consonant (consonant cluster) is Guru (G)
guru_conditions.vowel_before_anusvara: Vowel before anusvara (M in SLP1) is Guru (G)
guru_conditions.vowel_before_visarga: Vowel before visarga (H in SLP1) is Guru (G)
guru_conditions.final_syllable_with_consonant: Final syllable with trailing consonant(s) is Guru (G)

laghu_conditions.short_vowel: Short vowel (a, i, u, r, l, e, o) not in Guru conditions is Laghu (L)
laghu_conditions.vowel_not_followed_by_conjunct: Short vowel followed by only single consonant or space is Laghu (L)

slp1_special.description: Anusvara and visarga modify syllable weight

ambiguous_cases.nasal_before_cluster: Nasal (m, n, N, n) before consonant cluster - treat syllable as Guru if nasal perceived as part of closure
ambiguous_cases.final_syllable: Final syllable always considered based on its own vowel length and following segments
ambiguous_cases.closed_syllable: Syllable ending with consonant group (CVC pattern) is Guru even with short vowel

anushtubh.description: 8-syllable metre with pattern GGGG LGGG per quarter (pAda)
anushtubh.example: agnI medhA jushA RM / mayA mat_tam upA gam
anushtubh.notes: Most common metre in Sanskrit epics and Vedas
